Collapse several data rows per atlas region into one

Source: R/aggregate_values.R
aggregate_brain_values.Rd

Groups data by the columns that identify an atlas region and reduces every other column to a single value: numeric columns with fun, non-numeric columns to their first value. This is what lets a plotting function accept long data with several rows per region (e.g. one row per subject) and draw a single summarised value per region, rather than letting the last row win. ggseg::geom_brain() and ggseg3d::ggseg3d() both aggregate with it.

Usage

aggregate_brain_values(
  data,
  keys,
  fun = mean,
  ignore = character(),
  warn_collapse = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame of values to plot, carrying the keys columns.

keys

Character vector of columns identifying an atlas region, e.g. c("label", "hemi"). These are kept, never aggregated.

fun

Aggregating function for numeric columns. It must reduce a vector to a single value; mean (the default), median and max all do.

ignore

Columns to leave out of the result entirely: the atlas metadata columns the caller joins on anyway, plus the plotting system's own bookkeeping columns (for ggplot2: group, PANEL, flipped_aes).

warn_collapse

Whether to warn with warn_collapsed_rows() when rows actually collapse. Pass FALSE when the rows are the atlas's own identity rows rather than user data.

Value

One row per unique key combination, in order of first appearance, with the keys columns and the aggregated columns.

See also

warn_collapsed_rows()

Examples

thickness <- data.frame(
  label = c("lh_precentral", "lh_precentral", "lh_insula"),
  hemi = "left",
  subject = c("s01", "s02", "s01"),
  thickness = c(0.1, 0.9, 0.5)
)

aggregate_brain_values(thickness, c("label", "hemi"))
#> Warning: ! Several `data` rows map to the same atlas region; combining them with `fun`.
#> ℹ Before ggseg 3.0.0 these rows overplotted, so the last one won. Pass `fun =
#>   dplyr::last` to keep that behaviour.
#> ℹ Non-numeric columns take the first value regardless of `fun`.
#> This warning is displayed once per session.
#>           label hemi subject thickness
#> 1 lh_precentral left     s01       0.5
#> 2     lh_insula left     s01       0.5

aggregate_brain_values(thickness, c("label", "hemi"), fun = max)
#>           label hemi subject thickness
#> 1 lh_precentral left     s01       0.9
#> 2     lh_insula left     s01       0.5

# Drop a column instead of aggregating it
aggregate_brain_values(thickness, c("label", "hemi"), ignore = "subject")
#>           label hemi thickness
#> 1 lh_precentral left       0.5
#> 2     lh_insula left       0.5
